title: Knowledge check: Database Fundamentals for API Developers

questions.prompt: How should an API protect a business invariant across multiple database writes?
options: Rely only on frontend validation to prevent duplicate or invalid records.
Disable foreign keys and unique constraints to improve correctness.
Use a transaction with deliberate boundaries and enforce important invariants with database constraints.
Commit each write separately and hope later writes do not fail.
questions.answer_key: Use a transaction with deliberate boundaries and enforce important invariants with database constraints.
questions.explanation: Use a transaction with deliberate boundaries and enforce important invariants with database constraints. This is especially relevant to “Database Fundamentals for API Developers” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Database Fundamentals for API Developers”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Force a failure inside a multi-write transaction and check that integrity remains intact.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
questions.answer_key: Force a failure inside a multi-write transaction and check that integrity remains intact.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Database Fundamentals for API Developers”?
options: Related database updates can partially commit or rely only on client-side validation.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
questions.answer_key: Related database updates can partially commit or rely only on client-side validation.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
